newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close much weaker, outperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close much weaker, outperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much weaker but outperformed the U.S. market on Friday, as a sharp decline in U.S. Treasury prices spilled across the border, analysts said.

"Canada is just following the U.S., but you can tell that it's nothing domestic that's driving it because Canadian spreads are pushing further below the U.S.," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.23 to C$118.56 to yield 6.571 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1 - 15/32 to yield 6.64 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to seven basis points from six basis points at Thursday's close.

"Our market has been driven by events in the U.S. today. It looks like they've had some difficulty distributing this week's auctions in the U.S.," said Al Brownbridge, portfolio manager with Investors Group.
Canadian bonds weakened with U.S. Treasuries as the market turned lower on new supply, a battered dollar, hedge fund selling and technically driven trades.

In Canada the yield curve steepened, with some T-bill yields falling sharply. Analysts attributed the shift partly to Canada's employment report for July, which showed employment rose by a lower-than-expected 15,000 jobs.
"The short end is well supported with the employment report. People were saying that the Bank of Canada was going to hike rates," said Kalirai. "Those expectations were pared down," he said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.57 to C$108.70 to yield 6.058 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 30/32 to yield 6.37 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 31 basis points from 28 basis points at Thursday's close.
